body.name: Positive Fourier minimum-distance estimator
body.construction: For every \(a\in\mathcal A\), the observed density relative to \(\lambda^n\) is at least \(c_0/K^n\), because \(dP_\theta^a/d\lambda^n(y)=p_\theta^a(f^{-1}(y))/|\det Df(f^{-1}(y))|\) and every singular value of \(Df\) is at most \(K\). Put \(\ell_0=c_0/(2K^n)\), \(g_L^a(y)=\max\{N^{-1},\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\|\ell\|_\infty\le L_N}\widehat c_{a\ell}e^{\mathrm i\ell^\top y}\}\), and \(\widehat p_L^a(y)=\ell_0+(1-\ell_0)g_L^a(y)/\int g_L^a d\lambda^n\). This density integrates to one and remains at least \(c_0/(2K^n)\) after normalization. Enumerate a rational wrapped-spline sieve of mechanisms and lifts \(Az+u(z)\), with \(A\) in the bounded subset of \(GL(n,\mathbb Z)\), and retain only candidates certified by interval arithmetic to satisfy the class bounds, positive Jacobian, degree one, and the finite-type profile. Define \(\widehat\theta_N\) as a certified approximate minimizer of the complete-family Hellinger criterion against \((\widehat p_L^a:a\in\mathcal A)\).
